intro.title: Multi-Tab Auth Sync
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application that demonstrates how to keep a user's authentication status synchronized across multiple browser tabs. You will learn the core concept of using browser storage events to communicate state changes between tabs. The main technologies involved are Angular services, localStorage, and the window's storage event listener. By the end, you will understand how to create a seamless multi-tab experience where logging in or out in one tab automatically updates the auth state in all others.
intro.usecase: Multi-tab auth sync is essential for modern web applications where users frequently work across multiple browser tabs. Banking dashboards, e-commerce platforms, and collaborative tools like Google Workspace all require consistent authentication states across tabs. When a user logs out in one tab, all other tabs should immediately reflect this change to prevent unauthorized access. Similarly, session timeouts or permission changes must propagate instantly to maintain security and user experience. This pattern ensures users don't encounter confusing or insecure states when switching between tabs of the same application.
